entry.title: Ariba: Rejection approval flow doesn't trigger on IRs
entry.content:
Has anyone implemented a specific approval to trigger if someone in the IR approval flow clicks on Reject?

We've turned Application.Invoicing.RejectRequiresNoMoreApprovals to No and we've tried using InvoiceReconciliation.IsForReject and InvoiceReconciliation.cus_MarkforReject on our approval rules to have a specific approval after rejection. When using the testing tab of the IR Approval Flow, we see the wanted behavour.

But on the actual approvable document, unless something else is first changed in the IR, after clicking on Reject, the approval flow is not resubmitted and regenerated as we need it to. 

Ariba Support suggest to log a customisation request based on what's written at the bottom here: https://help.sap.com/docs/buying-invoicing/approval-process-management-guide/default-approval-process-for-invoice-reconciliation-documents-for-credit-memos-6b941434c1da101496f78f16a2c6b546

But this talks about adding an approval group to rejected IR documents without exceptions. In our cases, we have exceptions and that makes no difference.

I'm confused as to what sort of customisation will trigger the resubmit of the approval flow after the Reject button is pushed. If anyone here has enabled such a customisation, could you please describe it?

thanks

Cathy

entry.title: Ariba Invoicing / Central Invoice Management — "Manager of Last Approver"
entry.content:
We are configuring the supplier invoice approval workflow in SAP Ariba Invoicing alongside an S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition rollout and want to use the "Manager of Last Approver" step type. The help documentation confirms what the step does, but not how it works. We checked Help Portal, configuration guides, SAP Notes and this community without finding an answer.

1. Data source: Which system resolves "the manager"? The supervisor attribute on the Ariba user record, the hierarchy in SAP Cloud Identity Services, the manager relationship from S/4HANA Cloud (Manage Workforce / Employee Central), or something else? And is it evaluated when the flow is generated or when the step becomes active?

2. Fallback: What happens if no manager is maintained for the last approver — escalation to a default approver, silent skip, or error state? Is the fallback configurable, and where?

3. Duplicates: If the resolved manager already appears earlier in the chain, is the step skipped or does that person approve twice?

Thx

entry.title: SAP Ariba Invoicing (CIM): Process of Reverse Charge and implementation
entry.content:
Hello SAP Community,

I could not find any documentation regarding the Reverse Charge process in SAP Ariba Invoicing.

As I understand it, Reverse Charge is a VAT mechanism where the supplier does not charge VAT on the invoice. Instead, the customer is responsible for calculating, reporting, and paying the VAT to the tax authorities. In many B2B cross-border scenarios, the customer accounts for the VAT in their VAT return rather than the supplier charging it on the invoice. [In our scenario, an Austrian company purchases services from a German supplier (e.g. SAP).]

How can this scenario be implemented in CIM, considering that the available Business Rules do not work for this use case?

Additionally, according to the customer, the internal tax engine should not be used.

Could someone explain how to set up and handle this scenario in SAP Ariba Invoicing?

Thanks in advance for your support.

 

SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing
